title: EU Residency Sentinel: prioritized routing, tier-aware fallbacks, and customer allow/deny enforcement
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Implement a production-ready policy layer ("Sentinel") that enforces EU-only data residency constraints while still providing graceful capacity-aware fallbacks and honoring customer allowlists/denylists. The Sentinel will sit in the Smart Routing path and make per-request decisions using a deterministic precedence: 1) explicit customer denylist (block), 2) customer allowlist (pin to customer-scoped EU hosts), 3) residency constraints (route only to EU-qualified capacity), 4) tier routing (preferred hosted/dedicated/private), then 5) model-variant fallback (EU-quantized or EU-small models). We must avoid any cross-border egress for requests flagged as EU-residency and provide transparent telemetry when a fallback is applied.
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel evaluates routing policies for 100% of requests with residency metadata and returns an auditable decision record
Requests with customer denylist are rejected with 403 and explicit reason code; audit log contains denylist key and timestamp
Allowlisted customers are routed only to EU capacity (hosted/dedicated/private based on config) with pinning honored during rollouts

When EU capacity is saturated, Sentinel performs tier-aware fallback: prefer EU-dedicated burst capacity, then EU-quantized model-variant (compatible architecture), and only if customer opts-in allow cross-region fallback (opt-in stored on customer profile)
End-to-end integration tests (simulated EU-only requests, capacity saturation scenarios, allow/denylist changes) pass in CI and runbook created
Telemetry: per-decision metrics emitted (decision_reason, target_region, target_tier, model_variant, fallback_used) and dashboard created in Console
tasks: Design policy precedence and decision schema (policy_id, conditions, action, audit_code)
Extend PDP (policy decision service) API to accept residency metadata and customer ACLs
Implement routing adaptor layer to translate Sentinel decisions into router actions (region, tier, model_variant)
Add model-compatibility matrix for allowed fallback variants inside EU (quantized versions, smaller shards)
Write integration tests for saturation + fallback scenarios and replay harness for audit logs
Create Console dashboard and alerting for fallback rate > 1% and denylist hits

qa_plan: Create CI playground with synthetic tenants flagged for EU residency. Run nightly scenarios: (1) normal capacity, (2) EU saturation with dedicated burst available, (3) EU saturation without burst where fallback to quantized model is required, (4) denylist change in-flight. Validate no request is routed to non-EU hosts for residency=EU unless customer_opt_in=true. Include end-to-end latency regression guard (95p increase < 15%).
notes: Trade-offs discussed: 1) Adding a strict block for denylist vs returning a soft-warning — we chose strict block to reduce compliance risk. 2) Decided to prefer EU quantized model variants over cross-region routing to preserve residency; downside is potential quality regression monitored by Redwood Optimize evals. 3) To minimize latency increase, decision path kept in-memory cache with TTL=30s; must invalidate on ACL changes.
